SASRec’s sampler aligns input item x_t with positive x_(t+1); losses must exclude padded targets. Its predictor scores candidates from the final sequence feature, assuming right-aligned histories. Any added pooling branch used at every training position must pool only nonpadding items through that position; whole-sequence pooling leaks future interactions. [Reference sampler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/main/python/utils.py), [model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/main/python/model.py). PyTorch MultiheadAttention boolean masks use True to block attention: combine an upper-triangular future mask with padding-key exclusion. Padding queries need separate handling; fully masked rows can produce NaNs, so explicitly handle empty prefixes. Positional indexing must also remain consistent when checking padding invariance. [Attention documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.activation.MultiheadAttention.html), [masking caveat](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/intermediate/transformer_building_blocks.html).

The reference scales input item embeddings by sqrt(d), applies final LayerNorm, and scores against unscaled item embeddings. Preserve residual placement and avoid adding a residual twice when adapting feed-forward modules. For an added embedding-pooling branch, masked means and explicit normalization are reasonable design choices for comparable scales; validate them rather than assuming equivalence. A sigmoid gate with zero preactivation starts at 0.5, so it immediately changes the representation; a negative bias starts nearer the baseline for an additive gated branch. These are implementation deductions, not established HR improvements. Save architecture configuration alongside every parameter/buffer, reconstruct the same computation in the predictor writer, load strictly, and call eval(). Verify matching candidate logits within numerical tolerance after reload, including short and padded histories. [Reference architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/main/python/model.py), [PyTorch checkpoint guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html).
